```python
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 7  # sources
    J = 6  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [126, 87, 89, 219, 237, 83, 119]
    demands = [42, 36, 40, 26, 48, 13]
    cost_matrix = [[7.4, 26.17, 11.24, 22.0, 20.25, 26.16], [3.09, 10.57, 15.83, 27.45, 9.9, 24.32], [13.21, 17.6, 27.35, 4.35, 20.76, 13.87], [12.99, 22.77, 21.44, 16.55, 11.14, 11.42], [7.94, 20.58, 5.92, 26.51, 18.82, 12.66], [7.6, 11.65, 12.85, 26.18, 25.76, 13.93], [6.2, 12.61, 7.7, 3.86, 5.64, 26.29]]
    emission_matrix = [[13.77, 6.2, 15.2, 3.96, 15.4, 2.22], [11.74, 18.88, 13.83, 15.14, 15.29, 15.11], [13.01, 10.24, 11.99, 6.96, 15.14, 4.55], [9.73, 13.5, 7.46, 7.62, 16.24, 7.48], [5.7, 1.98, 4.99, 5.81, 3.09, 9.42], [9.44, 18.97, 4.13, 13.89, 1.0, 16.68], [20.0, 8.53, 9.6, 14.35, 5.23, 5.49]]
    fixed_costs = [[291, 134, 170, 292, 152, 152], [106, 108, 129, 205, 237, 97], [92, 174, 115, 222, 233, 115], [58, 123, 223, 144, 229, 249], [100, 207, 58, 231, 203, 113], [195, 164, 67, 78, 82, 160], [296, 108, 288, 152, 255, 170]]
    moq = [[7, 5, 13, 18, 18, 6], [19, 11, 18, 8, 7, 6], [17, 7, 11, 17, 19, 20], [15, 20, 17, 13, 9, 11], [17, 10, 7, 16, 19, 13], [8, 11, 20, 7, 5, 19], [12, 19, 16, 18, 18, 10]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

To: Executive Leadership Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Subject: Balancing transportation cost and carbon impact in store replenishment
Date: Today

Context
Our replenishment network must meet store service levels while advancing our climate commitments. Each potential shipping route between our warehouses and stores carries two key measures: the money we spend per unit shipped and the carbon we emit per unit shipped. These measures often pull in different directions—some of the lowest-cost lanes rely on modes or distances that drive higher emissions, while cleaner options may come at a higher unit cost. We need a pragmatic plan that delivers inventory on time, controls spend, and meaningfully reduces our footprint.

Operational rules we must respect
- Route activation costs: Turning on a route requires a one-time setup outlay (e.g., carrier onboarding, customs and paperwork, dock readiness). A route is either active or not; once active, this setup fee is incurred regardless of how much we ship.
- Minimum order quantities: Activated routes must move at least a defined minimum volume to justify the logistics overhead and ensure we’re not running partial loads.
- Supplier limits per store: For receiving efficiency and vendor management simplicity, each store may only receive from a limited number of warehouses within the planning horizon.

Network realities
- Warehouses cannot ship more than their available inventory. We must allocate outbound volume without exceeding supply at any location.
- Stores have defined minimum demand that must be met to protect in-stock targets. We must satisfy these requirements in full.
- Because some greener lanes may require more route activations or create longer-haul flows, we will evaluate whether the emissions gains justify any added fixed and variable costs, keeping the above rules intact.

Management priority
Leadership has set relative importance for cost versus emissions. We will honor these priorities by blending the two metrics. Variable shipping spend and total emissions will be combined using the importance weights set by management, and one-time route setup fees will be added in full (these fees are not scaled by the weights). This approach reflects our need to manage the P&L while progressing toward emissions reductions.

Goal
Identify which routes to activate and how much to ship on each active route, such that:
- Warehouse inventory is not exceeded and each store’s minimum demand is met
- Activated routes ship at or above their required minimum volume
- Each store receives from no more than the allowed number of warehouses
- The combined outcome—weighted variable cost plus weighted emissions, plus full setup fees—is as low as possible under the priorities set by management

Deliverable and decision support
We will produce a recommended shipping plan that lists active routes and ship quantities, with clear articulation of:
- Total transportation spend, total emissions, and the blended measure used for decision-making
- Store-level supplier assignments that respect the supplier limit
- Any trade-offs made to achieve better carbon outcomes without compromising service or breaching supply caps
We will also provide scenario runs to illustrate how the plan shifts if management adjusts the importance weights or if supply/demand inputs change.
